text:
Jordan Kim: Hey all - planning parental leave starting Mar 4 for ~12 weeks. Couple items: is there a caregiver credit (not just reimbursements) that covers evening/weekend help? Also want to set up a formal phased return (3 weeks at 50%, then 3 at 75%). What's the paperwork and who signs off?

people-ops-bot: Hi Jordan! See parental resources: https://intranet.redwood/people/parental-benefits. We support Backup Care reimbursements and a regional Care Credit pilot in some markets. Submit the parental intake form and select 'Care Credit' or 'Phased Return' to trigger teams.

Marcus Velez: @Jordan we run a Care Credit pilot in US/UK regions: one-time $900 credit applied to approved caregivers (licensed or vetted marketplace). It's separate from monthly reimbursements. Intake + receipts required. I can check eligibility once you submit.

Sofia Tran: For phased return, manager sign-off + a signed phased-return agreement needed. Manager documents expected hours and outcomes; People Ops configures payroll/benefits. Add expected weekly hours in the intake and choose effective dates.

Jordan Kim: Thanks. Does the Care Credit require pre-enrollment with a vendor or can I use any vetted sitter and submit receipts?

Marcus Velez: Either works. If you're using one of our vetted marketplace partners, the credit can apply at enrollment and reduce out-of-pocket. For independent caregivers, you submit receipts and we reimburse up to the credit amount.

Payroll Team: Note on payroll: phased return changes must be submitted at least 7 business days before payroll cut to take effect the following pay period. Care Credit is processed as a non-taxable benefit when receipts meet policy. If you request an advance, that may be handled separately.

Jordan Kim: I might need a small advance for initial weeks. Is that common? How fast does it process?

Benefits Team: We can approve a one-time childcare advance case-by-case up to $1,500. Processing is 3-7 business days after intake + manager approval. Attach an estimate of expected invoices in the intake to expedite.

Manager - Priya: I approve the phased-return in principle. Jordan, please drop a draft weekly schedule and we can finalize outcomes. Also tag any PRs or on-call ownership to reassign before you go.

Jordan Kim: Will do. On coverage: I have two recurring customer demos in week 4 and 7. Can someone volunteer to run them?

Sofia Tran: I can run week 4 demo and shadow the prep. @Marcus take week 7?

Marcus Velez: I can take week 7. Jordan, add the deck and key talking points to the invite and I'll rehearse.

Security Ops: FYI if you're traveling outside your home country on leave and plan to access company systems, file a short travel/access form. Otherwise use company laptop + MFA.

Jordan Kim: Noted. One more Q: how is performance handled during phased return? I don't want partial expectations causing a negative review.

Manager - Priya: We'll rebaseline objectives for the phased period and note in your calibration packet that you were on phased return. If you prefer, we can defer your end-of-cycle review until full return; note that in the intake and we'll flag it for People Ops.

Benefits Team: After intake, expect Care Credit eligibility confirmation in ~5 business days, phased-return paperwork in 3-5 business days after manager sign-off, and advance decisions within 3-7 business days. If you need anything faster, mark "expedite" on the intake.

Jordan Kim: Great — filing intake now and selecting Care Credit + phased-return. I'll post the schedule and demo decks here once uploaded. Thanks everyone! :raised_hands:
